comment: The bars ci/trees-figures.py holds the tree views' release figures to: the recording engine's budgets (ci/bench-budget.json, docs/performance.md). A gated figure (`"gate": true`: the many-file `create`) that misses its bar fails the tracer; every other missed bar is a warning. Every workload has its own `deadline_s` and reports what it reached by then; nothing is extrapolated. A workload misses its bar when it does not finish by its deadline, or when its `metric` is over `max` (one number, or one per filesystem), or any of its `metrics` is over its own max. `create` runs for half the engine's 600 s and is held to half its 100,000 creates, the engine's rate of 6 ms a create. `close_64m` is held, unscaled, to the engine's close of a dirty 1 GiB file, and `close_1g` to the same, at its size: the close and stat after the writes. `write_1g` holds the same run's last 64 writes to 1.5 times a 1 MiB file's write. `history_1g` holds that save's drain to 60 s, the engine's own 1 GiB commit (23 to 29 s) with margin, and `memory_1g` the view's peak through it to 256 MiB over its memory before, whatever the file's size. `memory_create` holds the view's peak through the `create` workload and its build, over its memory before, to 2 KiB a file it left. Every memory figure is the sampled peak of the view's RssAnon (anonymous resident memory, read from /proc/PID/status through the workload and its build; clean file-backed git index pages are not counted, owner 2026-11-20). The memory and stall figures warn and never fail, and their numbers are marks for regressions, not targets (owner, 2026-11-20: "I dont have a number in mind. Im just looking to cut waste"): `close_frag` holds the longest hold of the volume's actor lock through a 64 MiB file's close after 200,000 random 64-byte writes to 50 ms (stages.actor_lock.max_nanos, the process's maximum: only a run with `--only close_frag` holds that close alone), `write_1m` the view's peak through a close of 1,000,000 64-byte appends and its build to 256 MiB over its memory before, `restart` the view mounted again on the state the figures left (about 50,000 files) to 15 s and a 256 MiB peak from its start to its mount, and `long_history` 2,000 more creates on it to 1.2 times the ms a create of `create`'s first 2,000 took. `grace_s` is how long a save the deadline caught may run on before the view's connection is aborted.

close_64m.text: within the engine's close of a dirty 1 GiB file, 12 s on ext4 and 8 s on XFS (bigclose)

close_1g.text: the engine's close of a dirty 1 GiB file, 12 s on ext4 and 8 s on XFS (bigclose, dirty)

history_1g.text: the 1 GiB save built within 60 s of its close (the engine's own 1 GiB commit takes 23 to 29 s)

memory_1g.text: the view's peak memory through the 1 GiB save and its build under 256 MiB over its memory before. It is the sampled peak of the view's RssAnon (anonymous resident memory, what the kernel cannot reclaim), warns and never fails, and is a mark for regressions, not a target (owner, 2026-11-20: "I dont have a number in mind. Im just looking to cut waste")

memory_create.text: the view's peak memory through the create workload and its build over its memory before, at most 2 KiB a file it left (a 100,000-file tree in under 200 MiB). It is the sampled peak of the view's RssAnon (anonymous resident memory, what the kernel cannot reclaim), warns and never fails, and is a mark for regressions, not a target (owner, 2026-11-20: "I dont have a number in mind. Im just looking to cut waste")

write_1g.text: the last 64 1 MiB writes of a 1 GiB file, median within 1.5 times a 1 MiB file's write

close_frag.text: the longest hold of the actor lock through a 64 MiB file's close after 200,000 random 64-byte writes, at most 50 ms (read alone with --only close_frag: a full run's maximum is the whole process's)

write_1m.text: the view's peak memory through a close of 1,000,000 64-byte appends in one open, and its build, under 256 MiB over its memory before. It is the sampled peak of the view's RssAnon (anonymous resident memory, what the kernel cannot reclaim), warns and never fails, and is a mark for regressions, not a target (owner, 2026-11-20: "I dont have a number in mind. Im just looking to cut waste")

restart.text: the view mounted again on the figures' state (about 50,000 files) within 15 s, its peak memory from its start to its mount under 256 MiB. It is the sampled peak of the view's RssAnon (anonymous resident memory, what the kernel cannot reclaim), warns and never fails, and is a mark for regressions, not a target (owner, 2026-11-20: "I dont have a number in mind. Im just looking to cut waste")

long_history.text: 2,000 creates on the restarted view, at most 1.2 times the ms a create of the create workload's first 2,000 took
